Playbook.name: Change Audit — Windows Network Share Created, Modified or Deleted - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A network share was created, modified or deleted (5142/5143/5144). Triage question: is this authorised share administration, or an attacker creating an exposure/exfil share or removing evidence of one?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Rogue shares expose data or provide an exfil channel; deleting a share can hide lateral-movement infrastructure.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the share change is authorised administration or the creation/removal of a rogue share.

Step.name: Detail the share change and actor
Step.Purpose: Identify the share name, path, actor and whether several shares were changed at once.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("5142","5143","5144") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.ShareName, winlog.event_data.ShareLocalPath | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: A share on a sensitive path (C:\, Windows, user profiles) created by a non-admin is concerning. Admin shares (C$/ADMIN$) are default; a NEW named share pointing at a broad path is the exposure risk.

Step.name: Is the actor an admin, and did they change shares on multiple hosts
Step.Purpose: Broad share changes by one principal across hosts indicate scripted attacker activity vs a single admin task.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("5142","5143","5144") AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS changes = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), shares = VALUES(winlog.event_data.ShareName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many hosts/shares by one actor in minutes = scripted. One change by a known admin = routine.

Node.Condition: A new share on a sensitive/broad path created by a non-admin, or shares changed across multiple hosts by one actor.
A known admin creating/adjusting an expected share under a change record.
Share deletion that removes a previously-flagged rogue share (cleanup) - benign but note.
Share change by a plausible admin with no change record.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SHARE-CHANGE, INV-02-SHARE-ACTOR to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Creation of a rogue exposure/exfil share or removal of evidence.

Indicators.Item: New share on a broad/sensitive path by a non-admin.
Share points at data of value.

SOCAction.Item: Remove the rogue share; inspect what it exposed; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automation/provisioning tool managing shares unexpectedly.

Indicators.Item: A known provisioning account per a broken job.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
